speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
iast:
dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya
english_telang: What did my (people) and the Pāṇḍavas do, O Sañjaya! when they assembled together on the holy field of Kurukṣetra , desirous to do battle?

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
सञ्जय उवाच।
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा।
आचार्यमुपसंगम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
iast:
sañjaya uvāca
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā
ācāryamupasaṃgamya rājā vacanamabravīt
english_telang: Seeing the army of the Pāṇḍavas drawn up in battle-array the prince Duryodhana approached the preceptor

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता ॥
iast:
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm
vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
english_telang: and spoke (these) words: 'O preceptor! observe this grand army of the sons of Pāṇḍu drawn up in battle-array by your talented pupil the son of Drupada. In it are heroes (bearing) large bows

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः ॥
iast:
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi
yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ
english_telang: the equals of Bhīma and Arjuna in battle—(namely) Yuyudhāna Virāṭa and Drupada the master of a great car and Dhṛṣṭaketu

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुंगवः ॥
iast:
dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān
purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṃgavaḥ
english_telang: Cekitāna and the valiant king of Kāsī Purujit and Kuntibhoja

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः ॥
iast:
yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān
saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ
english_telang: and that eminent man Śaibya the heroic Yudhāmanyu, the valiant Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadrā , and the sons of Draupadī—all masters of great cars. And now, O best of Brāhmaṇas!

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
iast:
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tānbravīmi te
english_telang: learn who are most distinguished among us, and are leaders of my army. I will name them to you, in order that you may know them well. Yourself, and Bhīṣma, and Karṇa , and Kṛpa the victor of (many) battles Aśvatthāman

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च ॥
iast:
bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiñjayaḥ
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca
english_telang: and Vikarṇa and also the son of Somadatta

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः ॥
iast:
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english_telang: and many other brave men who have given up their lives for me who fight with various weapons, (and are) all dexterous in battle.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम् ॥
iast:
aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam
paryāptaṃ tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam
english_telang: Thus our army which is protected by Bhīṣma is unlimited

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि ॥
iast:
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ
bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi
english_telang: while this army of theirs which is protected by Bhīma is very limited. And therefore do ye all, occupying respectively the positions assigned to you, protect Bhīṣma only.'

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः।
सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥
iast:
tasya sañjanayanharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ
siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
english_telang: Then his powerful grandsire Bhīṣma the oldest of the Kauravas roaring aloud like a lion blew his conch, (thereby) affording delight to Duryodhana. And then all at once

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ॥
iast:
tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ
sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo.abhavat
english_telang: conchs and kettledrums and tabors

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः ॥
iast:
tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
english_telang: and trumpets were played upon and there was a tumultuous din. Then, too, Mādhava and the son of Pāṇḍu (Arjuna), seated in a grand chariot to which white steeds were yoked, blew their heavenly conchs.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनञ्जयः।
पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः ॥
iast:
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
english_telang: Hṛṣīkeśa blew the Pāñcajanya, and Dhanañjaya the Devadatta, and Bhīma, (the doer) of fearful deeds, blew the great conch Pauṇḍra . King Yudhiṣṭhira

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ ॥
iast:
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
english_telang: the son of Kuntī blew the Anantavijaya and Nakula and Sahadeva (respectively) the Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka. And the king of Kāśī too who has an excellent bow and Sikhaṇḍin the master of a great car and Dhṛṣṭadyumna

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः ॥
iast:
kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ
dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ
english_telang: Virāṭa

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
iast:
drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate
saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak
english_telang: and the unconquered Sātyaki and Drupada and the sons of Draupadī and the son of Subhadrā of mighty arms blew conchs severally from all sides

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलोऽभ्यनुनादयन् (or लोव्यनु) ॥
iast:
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat
nabhaśca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo.abhyanunādayan (lo vyanu)
english_telang: O king of the earth! That tumultuous din rent the hearts of all (the people) of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's (party)

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान् कपिध्वजः।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः।
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते ॥
iast:
atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ
pravṛtte śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
english_telang: causing reverberations throughout heaven and earth. Then seeing (the people of ) Dhṛtarāṣṭra's party regularly marshalled the son of Pāṇḍu whose standard is the ape raised his bow after the discharge of missiles had commenced

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत ॥
iast:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate
arjuna uvāca
senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me.acyuta
english_telang: and O king of the earth! spake these words to Hṛṣīkeśa: 'O undegraded one! station my chariot between the two armies while I observe those who stand here desirous to engage in battle and with whom in the labours of this struggle I must do battle. I will observe those who are assembled here and who are about to engage in battle, wishing to do service in battle to the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.' Thus addressed by Guḍākeśa, O descendant of Bharata!

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्।
कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे ॥
iast:
yāvadetānnirikṣe.ahaṃ yoddhukāmānavasthitān
kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasmin raṇasamudyame
english_telang: Hṛṣīkeśa stationed that excellent chariot between the two armies in front of Bhīṣma and Droṇa and of all the kings of the earth

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः।
धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः ॥
iast:
yotsyamānānavekṣe.ahaṃ ya ete.atra samāgatāḥ
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
english_telang: and said O son of Pṛthā! look at these assembled Kauravas.'

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata
senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
english_telang: There the son of Pṛthā saw in both armies fathers and grandfathers preceptors maternal uncles brothers

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति ॥
iast:
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām
uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti
english_telang: sons

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितॄनथ पितामहान्।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातॄन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा ॥
iast:
tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṝnatha pitāmahān
ācāryānmātulānbhrātṛnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā
english_telang: grandsons

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि।
तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान् ॥
iast:
śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi
tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān
english_telang: companions fathers-in-law as well as friends. And seeing all those kinsmen standing (there) the son of Kuntī was overcome by excessive pity

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कृपया परयाविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।
अर्जुन उवाच।
दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
iast:
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt
arjuna uvāca
dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam
english_telang: and spake thus despondingly. Seeing these kinsmen, O Kṛṣṇa ! standing (here) desirous to engage in battle, my limbs droop down my mouth is quite dried up a tremor comes on my body

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
iast:
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati
vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate
english_telang: and my hairs stand on end

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
iast:
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate
na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
english_telang: the Gāṇḍīva (bow) slips from my hand my skin burns intensely. I am unable, too, to stand up my mind whirls round, as it were

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे ॥
iast:
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava
na ca śreyo.anupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave
english_telang: O Keśava! I see adverse omens and I do not perceive any good (to accrue) after killing (my) kinsmen in the battle.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
iast:
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā
english_telang: I do not wish for victory, O Kṛṣṇa! nor sovereignty, nor pleasures: what is sovereignty to us, O Govinda ! what enjoyments, and even life? Even those

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
iast:
yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca
ta ime.avasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca
english_telang: for whose sake we desire sovereignty enjoyments and pleasures are standing here for battle abandoning life and wealth-preceptors fathers

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः।
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा ॥
iast:
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinastathā
english_telang: sons as well as grandfathers maternal uncles fathers-in-law grandsons brothers-in-law as also (other) relatives.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
iast:
etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato.api madhusūdana
api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte
english_telang: These I do not wish to kill though they kill (me) O destroyer of Madhu! even for the sake of sovereignty over the three worlds how much less then for this earth (alone)?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।
पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः ॥
iast:
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana
pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ
english_telang: What joy shall be ours, O Janārdana ! after killing Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons? Killing these felons we shall only incur sin.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
iast:
tasmānnārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān
svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
english_telang: Therefore it is not proper for us to kill our own kinsmen the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. For how O Mādhava! shall we be happy after killing our own relatives?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
iast:
yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam
english_telang: Although having their consciences corrupted by avarice they do not see the evils flowing from the extinction of a family and the sin in treachery to friends still

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
iast:
kathaṃ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum
kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana
english_telang: O Ganārdana! should not we

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
iast:
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo.abhibhavatyuta
english_telang: who do see the evils flowing from the extinction of a family learn to refrain from that sin? On the extinction of a family

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥
iast:
adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ
english_telang: the eternal rites of families are destroyed. Those rites being destroyed, impiety predominates over the whole family. In consequence of the predominance of impiety, O Kṛṣṇa! the women of the family become corrupt and the women becoming corrupt, O descendant of Vṛṣṇi! intermingling of castes results

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
iast:
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca
patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
english_telang: that intermingling necessarily leads the family and the destroyers of the family to hell for when the ceremonies of (offering) the balls of food and water (to them) fail, their ancestors fall down (to hell). By these transgressions of the destroyers of families which occasion interminglings of castes

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
iast:
doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ
utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ
english_telang: the eternal rites of castes and rites

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन।
नरके नियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम (or नरकेऽनियतं) ॥
iast:
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana
narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma
english_telang: of families are subverted. And O Janārdana! we have heard that men whose family-rites are subverted

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्।
यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
iast:
aho bata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam
yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ
english_telang: must necessarily live in hell. Alas! we are engaged in committing a heinous sin, seeing that we are making efforts for killing our own kinsmen out of greed of the pleasures of sovereignty.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः।
धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
iast:
yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet
english_telang: If the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapon in hand, should kill me in battle, me weaponless and not defending (myself), that would be better for me.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्त्वार्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamuktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ
english_telang: Having spoken thus, Arjuna cast aside his bow together with the arrows, on the battle-field, and sat down in (his) chariot, with a mind agitated by grief.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
सञ्जय उवाच।
तं तथा कृपयाविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम्।
विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
iast:
sañjaya uvāca
taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭamaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam
viṣīdantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ
english_telang: To him, who was thus overcome with pity, and dejected, and whose eyes were full of tears and turbid, the destroyer of Madhu spoke these words. How (comes it that) this delusion O Arjuna ! which is discarded by the good

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam
anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna
english_telang: which excludes from heaven

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
iast:
klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate
kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
english_telang: and occasions infamy has overtaken you in this (place of) peril? Be not effeminate, O son of Pṛthā! it is not worthy of you. Cast off this base weakness of heart, and arise, O terror of (your) foes!

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṅkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana
iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana
english_telang: How, O destroyer of Madhu! shall I encounter with arrows in the battle Bhīṣma and Droṇa —both, O destroyer of enemies! entitled to reverence?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
iast:
gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyamapīha loke
hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
english_telang: Not killing (my) preceptors—(men) of great glory—it is better to live even on alms in this world. But killing them though they are avaricious of worldly goods I should only enjoy blood-tainted enjoyments. Nor do we know which of the two is better for us-whether that we should vanquish them

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो
यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः।
यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्-
तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
iast:
na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāmaḥ te.avasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
english_telang: or that they should vanquish us. Even those

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः
पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे
शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
iast:
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ
yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste.ahaṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
english_telang: whom having killed we do not wish to live—even those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra stand (arrayed) against us. With a heart contaminated by the taint of helplessness with a mind confounded about my duty I ask you. Tell me what is assuredly good for me. I am your disciple instruct me

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्
यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
iast:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam
english_telang: who have thrown myself on your (indulgence). For I do not perceive what is to dispel that grief which will dry up my organs after I shall have obtained a prosperous kingdom on earth without a foe or even the sovereignty of the gods.

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ
na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
english_telang: Having spoken thus to Hriṣīkesa, O terror of (your) foes! Guḍākeśa said to Govinda , 'I shall not engage in battle;' and verily remained silent. To him thus desponding between the two armies, O descendant of Bharata!

speaker: Sanjaya
devanagari:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
iast:
tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata
senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṃ vacaḥ
english_telang: Hṛṣīkesa spoke these words with a slight smile.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase
gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
english_telang: You have grieved for those who deserve no grief, and you talk words of wisdom. Learned men grieve not for the living nor the dead. Never did I not exist, nor you, nor these rulers of men

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
iast:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
english_telang: nor will any one of us ever hereafter cease to be. As

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
dehino.asminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā
tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati
english_telang: in this body infancy and youth and old age (come) to the embodied (self) so does the acquisition of another body a sensible man is not deceived about that The contacts of the senses

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
iast:
mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ
āgamāpāyino.anityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata
english_telang: O son of Kuntī ! which produce cold and heat pleasure and pain are not permanent they are ever coming and going.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so.amṛtatvāya kalpate
english_telang: Bear them, O descendant of Bharata! For, O chief of men! that sensible man whom they (pain and pleasure being alike to him) afflict not, he merits immortality.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
iast:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo.antastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ
english_telang: There is no existence for that which is unreal there is no non-existence for that which is real. And the (correct) conclusion about both is perceived by those who perceive the truth.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥
iast:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati
english_telang: Know that to be indestructible which pervades all this the destruction of that inexhaustible (principle) none can bring about.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
iast:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ
anāśino.aprameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata
english_telang: These bodies appertaining to the embodied (self) which is eternal, indestructible, and indefinable, are said to be perishable therefore do engage in battle, O descendant of Bharata!

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
iast: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
english_telang: He who thinks it to be the killer and he who thinks it to be killed, both know nothing. It kills not, is not killed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्
नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato.ayaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
english_telang: It is not born, nor does it ever die, nor, having existed, does it exist no more. Unborn, everlasting, unchangeable, and primeval, it is not killed when the body is killed. O son of Pṛthā! how can that man who knows it thus to be indestructible everlasting unborn

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
iast:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
english_telang: and inexhaustible how and whom can he kill whom can he cause to be killed? As a man

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा-
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
iast:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro.aparāṇi
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāni anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
english_telang: casting off old clothes puts on others and new ones so the embodied (self) casting off old bodies goes to others and new ones.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
iast:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
english_telang: Weapons do not divide it (into pieces) fire does not burn it, waters do not moisten it the wind does not dry it up. It is not divisible it is not combustible it is not to be moistened

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
iast:
acchedyo.ayamadāhyo.ayamakledyo.aśoṣya eva ca
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo.ayaṃ sanātanaḥ
english_telang: it is not to be dried up. It is everlasting, all-pervading, stable, firm, and eternal.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
avyakto.ayamacintyo.ayamavikāryo.ayamucyate
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
english_telang: It is said to be unperceived, to be unthinkable, to be unchangeable. Therefore knowing it to be such

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
english_telang: you ought not to grieve But even if you think that it is constantly born and constantly dies still O you of mighty arms! you ought not to grieve thus. For to one that is born

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
tasmādaparihārye.arthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
english_telang: death is certain and to one that dies, birth is certain. Therefore about (this) unavoidable thing, you ought not to grieve. The source of things, O descendant of Bharata! is unperceived

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
iast:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
english_telang: their middle state is perceived and their end again is unperceived. What (occasion is there for any) lamentation regarding them?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन-
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥
iast:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenam āścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
english_telang: One looks upon it as a wonder another similarly speaks of it as a wonder another too hears of it as a wonder and even after having heard of it, no one does really know it.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
dehī nityamavadhyo.ayaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
english_telang: This embodied (self), O descendant of Bharata! within every one's body is ever indestructible. Therefore you ought not to grieve for any being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
iast:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo.anyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
english_telang: Having regard to your own duty also, you ought not to falter, for there is nothing better for a Kṣatriya than a righteous battle.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
iast:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
english_telang: Happy those Kṣatriyas O son of Pṛthā! who can find such a battle (to fight)—come of itself—an open door to heaven! But if you will not fight this righteous battle

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
english_telang: then you will have abandoned your own duty and your fame and you will incur sin.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te.avyayām
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
english_telang: All beings, too, will tell of your everlasting infamy and to one who has been honoured, infamy is (a) greater (evil) than death.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
english_telang: (Warriors who are) masters of great cars will think that you abstained from the battle through fear and having been highly thought of by them

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english_telang: you will fall down to littleness. Your enemies, too, decrying your power, will speak much about you that should not be spoken. And what, indeed, more lamentable than that?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
english_telang: Killed, you will obtain heaven victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore arise, O son of Kuntī! resolved to (engage in) battle.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi
english_telang: Looking alike on pleasure and pain, on gain and loss, on victory and defeat, then prepare for battle, and thus you will not incur sin.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
iast:
eṣā te.abhihitā sāṅkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
english_telang: The knowledge here declared to you is that relating to the Sāṅkhya,. Now hear that relating to the Yoga . Possessed of this knowledge, O son of Pṛthā! you will cast off the bonds of action. In this (path to final emancipation) nothing that is commenced becomes abortive

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
iast:
nehābhikramanāśo.asti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
english_telang: no obstacles exist and even a little of this (form of ) piety protects one from great danger.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
iast:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo.avyavasāyinām
english_telang: There is here O descendant of Kuru ! but one state of mind consisting in firm understanding. But the states of mind of those who have no firm understanding are many-branched and endless. The state of mind consisting in firm understanding regarding steady contemplation does not belong to those O son of Pṛthā! who are strongly attached to (worldly) pleasures and power and whose minds are drawn away by that flowery talk which is full of (ordinances of) specific acts for the attainment of (those) pleasures and (that) power and which promises birth as the fruit of acts—(that flowery talk) which those unwise ones utter who are enamoured of Vedic words

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
english_telang: who say there is nothing else

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
iast:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
english_telang: who are full of desires and whose goal is heaven.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
english_telang: The Vedas (merely) relate to the effects of the three qualities

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
iast:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
english_telang: do you O Arjuna! rise above those effects of the three qualities and be free from the pairs of opposites always preserve courage be free from anxiety for new acquisitions or protection of old acquisitions

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
iast:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
english_telang: and be self-controlled. To the instructed Brāhmaṇa there is in all the Vedas as much utility as in a reservoir of water into which waters flow from all sides.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo.astvakarmaṇi
english_telang: Your business is with action alone not by any means with fruit. Let not the fruit of action be your motive (to action). Let not your attachment be (fixed) on inaction.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
iast:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
english_telang: Having recourse to devotion, O Dhanañjaya ! perform actions, casting off (all) attachment, and being equable in success or ill-success (such) equability is called devotion.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
english_telang: Action, O Dhanañjaya! is far inferior to the devotion of the mind. In that devotion seek shelter. Wretched are those whose motive (to action) is the fruit (of action).

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
iast:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
english_telang: He who has obtained devotion in this world casts off both merit and sin. Therefore apply yourself to devotion devotion in (all) actions is wisdom.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
iast:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam
english_telang: The wise who have obtained devotion cast off the fruit of action and released from the shackles of (repeated)births repair to that seat where there is no unhappiness. When your mind shall have crossed beyond the taint of delusion then will you become indifferent to all that you have heard or will heard. When your mind

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
iast:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
english_telang: confounded by what you have heard

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
english_telang: will stand firm and steady in contemplation

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
english_telang: then will you acquire devotion. What are the characteristics, O Kesava! of one whose mind is steady, and who is intent on contemplation? How should one of steady mind speak, how sit, how move?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान्।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
english_telang: When a man O son of Pṛthā! abandons all the desires of his heart and is pleased in his self only and by his self he is then called one of steady mind.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
iast:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
english_telang: He whose heart is not agitated in the midst of calamities who has no longing for pleasures and from whom (the feelings of) affection fear and wrath have departed is called a sage of steady mind.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english_telang: His mind is steady, who, being without attachments anywhere, feels no exultation and no aversion on encountering the various agreeable and disagreeable (things of this world).

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo.aṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english_telang: A man's mind is steady, when he withdraws his senses from (all) objects of sense, as the tortoise (withdraws) its limbs from all sides.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
iast:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasavarjaṃ raso.apyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
english_telang: Objects of sense draw back from a person who is abstinent not so the taste (for those objects). But even the taste departs from him, when he has seen the Supreme.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
iast:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
english_telang: The boisterous senses, O son of Kuntī! carry away by force the mind even of a wise man, who exerts himself (for final emancipation).

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english_telang: Restraining them all, a man should remain engaged in devotion, making me his only resort. For his mind is steady whose senses are under his control.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
iast:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate
saṅgātsañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho.abhijāyate
english_telang: The man who ponders over objects of sense forms an attachment to them from (that) attachment is produced desire and from desire anger is produced

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
iast:
krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ
smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
english_telang: from anger results want of discrimination from want of discrimination, confusion of the memory from confusion of the memory, loss of reason

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
रागद्वेषविमुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् | (or वियुक्तैस्तु)
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
rāgadveṣavimuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran
orviyuktaistu ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
english_telang: and in consequence of loss of reason. he is utterly ruined. But the self-restrained man who moves among objects with senses under the control of his own self and free from affection and aversion obtains tranquillity. When there is tranquillity

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
iast:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
english_telang: all his miseries are destroyed for the mind of him whose heart is tranquil soon becomes steady.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
iast:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
english_telang: He who is not self-restrained has no steadiness of mind nor has he who is not self-restrained perseverance in the pursuit of self-knowledge there is no tranquillity for him who does not persevere in the pursuit of self-knowledge and whence can there be happiness for one who is not tranquil? For the heart which follows the rambling senses leads away his judgment

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
iast:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano.anuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
english_telang: as the wind leads a boat astray upon the waters.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
english_telang: Therefore, O you of mighty arms! his mind is steady whose senses are restrained on all sides from objects of sense.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
english_telang: The self-restrained man is awake, when it is night for all beings and when all beings are awake, that is the night of the right-seeing sage.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं
समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे
स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
iast:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
english_telang: He into whom all objects of desire enter, as waters enter the ocean, which, (though) replenished, (still) keeps its position unmoved,-he only obtains tranquillity not he who desires (those) objects of desire.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati
english_telang: The man who, casting off all desires, lives free from attachments, who is free from egoism, and from (the feeling that this or that is) mine, obtains tranquillity.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyāmantakāle.api brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
english_telang: This, O son of Pṛthā! is the Brahmic state attaining to this, one is never deluded and remaining in it in (one's) last moments, one attains ( brahma - nirvāṇa ) the Brahmic bliss.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
english_telang: If, O Ganārdana! devotion is deemed by you to be superior to action, then why, O Kesava! do you prompt me to (this) fearful action?

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
iast:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me
tadekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo.ahamāpnuyām
english_telang: You seem, indeed, to confuse my mind by equivocal words. Therefore, declare one thing determinately, by which I may attain the highest good.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
loke.asmina dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām
english_telang: O sinless one! I have already declared, that in this world there is a twofold path—that of the Sāṅkhyas by devotion in the shape of (true) knowledge and that of the Yogins by devotion in the shape of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo.aśnute
na ca saṃnyasanādeva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati
english_telang: A man does not attain freedom from action merely by not engaging in action nor does he attain perfection by mere renunciation. For nobody ever remains even for an instant without performing some action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
iast:
na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt
kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ
english_telang: since the qualities of nature constrain everybody, not having free-will (in the matter), to some action. The deluded man who

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
english_telang: restraining the organs of action continues to think in his mind about objects of sense is called a hypocrite. But he

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate.arjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
english_telang: O Arjuna ! who restraining his senses by his mind. and being free from attachments engages in devotion (in the shape) of action with the organs of action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
iast:
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
english_telang: is far superior. Do you perform prescribed action, for action is better than inaction, and the support of your body, too, cannot be accomplished with inaction.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥
iast:
yajñārthātkarmaṇo.anyatra loko.ayaṃ karmabandhanaḥ
tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara
english_telang: This world is fettered by all action other than action for the purpose of the sacrifice. Therefore, O son of Kuntī ! do you, casting off attachment, perform action for that purpose.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
iast:
sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo.astviṣṭakāmadhuk
english_telang: The Creator, having in olden times created men together with the sacrifice, said: 'Propagate with this. May it be the giver to you of the things you desire.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
iast:
devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha
english_telang: Please the gods with this, and may those gods please you. Pleasing each other you will attain the highest good. For pleased with the sacrifices

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
iast:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ
tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
english_telang: the gods will give you the enjoyments you desire. And he who enjoys himself without giving them what they have given is indeed a thief.'

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
iast:
yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
english_telang: The good who eat the leavings of a sacrifice are released from all sins. But the unrighteous ones who prepare food for themselves only

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
iast:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ
yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
english_telang: incur sin. From food are born (all) creatures from rain is the production of food rain is produced by sacrifices sacrifices are the result of action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
iast:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
english_telang: know that action has its source in the Vedas the Vedas come from the Indestructible. Therefore the all-comprehending Vedas are always concerned with sacrifices.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
iast:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
english_telang: He who in this world does not turn round the wheel revolving thus is of sinful life indulging his senses

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
iast:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
english_telang: and O son of Pṛthā! he lives in vain. But the man who is attached to his self only who is contented in his self and is pleased with his self has nothing to do.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
iast:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ
english_telang: He has no interest at all in what is done, and none whatever in what is not done, in this world nor is any interest of his dependent on any being.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
iast:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
english_telang: Therefore always perform action, which must be performed, without attachment. For a man, performing action without attachment, attains the Supreme.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
iast:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi sampaśyankartumarhasi
english_telang: By action alone, did Janaka and the rest work for perfection. And having regard also to the keeping of people (to their duties) you should perform action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
iast:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ
sa yatpramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate
english_telang: Whatever a great man does, that other men also do. And people follow whatever he receives as authority.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
iast:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana
nānavāptamavāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi
english_telang: There is nothing, O son of Pṛthā! for me to do in (all) the three worlds, nothing to acquire which has not been acquired. Still I do engage in action. For should I at any time not engage without sloth in action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
iast:
yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
english_telang: men would follow in my path from all sides

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।
सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
iast:
utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham
saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ
english_telang: O son of Pṛthā! If I did not perform actions, these worlds would be destroyed, I should be the cause of caste interminglings and I should be ruining these people. As the ignorant act

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
iast:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryādvidvāṃstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṃgraham
english_telang: O descendant of Bharata! with attachment to action so should a wise man act without attachment

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
iast:
na buddhibhedaṃ janayedajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām
joṣayetsarvakarmāṇi vidvānyuktaḥ samācaran
english_telang: wishing to keep the people (to their duties). A wise man should not shake the convictions of the ignorant who are attached to action but acting with devotion (himself ) should make them apply themselves to all action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।
अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते ॥
iast:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ
ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartāhamiti manyate
english_telang: He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks himself the doer of the actions which

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
iast:
tattvavittu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
english_telang: in every way are done by the qualities of nature. But he O you of mighty arms! who knows the truth about the difference from qualities and the difference from actions forms no attachments

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
iast:
prakṛterguṇasammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu
tānakṛtsnavido mandānkṛtsnavinna vicālayet
english_telang: believing that qualities deal with qualities. But those who are deluded by the qualities of nature form attachments to the actions of the qualities. A man of perfect knowledge should not shake these men of imperfect knowledge (in their convictions).

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
iast:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā
nirāśīrnirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ
english_telang: Dedicating all actions to me with a mind knowing the relation of the supreme and individual self engage in battle without desire without (any feeling that this or that is) mine and without any mental trouble.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
iast:
ye me matamidaṃ nityamanutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ
śraddhāvanto.anasūyanto mucyante te.api karmabhiḥ
english_telang: Even those men who always act on this opinion of mine full of faith and without carping are released from all actions. But those who carp at my opinion and do not act upon it

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
iast:
ye tvetadabhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam
sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃstānviddhi naṣṭānacetasaḥ
english_telang: know them to be devoid of discrimination deluded as regards all knowledge

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
iast:
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛterjñānavānapi
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
english_telang: and ruined. Even a man of knowledge acts consonantly to his own nature. All beings follow nature. What will restraint effect?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
iast:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau
tayorna vaśamāgacchettau hyasya paripanthinau
english_telang: Every sense has its affections and aversions towards its objects fixed. One should not become subject to them, for they are one's opponents.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
iast:
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt
svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ
english_telang: One's own duty, though defective, is better than another's duty well performed. Death in (performing) one's own duty is preferable the (performance of the) duty of others is dangerous.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
atha kena prayukto.ayaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ
anicchannapi vārṣṇeya balādiva niyojitaḥ
english_telang: But by whom, O descendant of Vṛṣṇi! is man impelled, even though unwilling, and, as it were, constrained by force, to commit sin? The Deity said:

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ
mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhyenamiha vairiṇam
english_telang: It is desire, it is wrath, born from the quality of passion it is very ravenous, very sinful. Know that that is the foe in this world. As fire is enveloped by smoke

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
iast:
dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathādarśo malena ca
yatholbenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtam
english_telang: a mirror by dust

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
iast:
āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā
kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca
english_telang: the fœtus by the womb so is this enveloped by desire. Knowledge, O son of Kuntī! is enveloped by this constant foe of the man of knowledge, in the shape of desire, which is like a fire and insatiable.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
iast:
indriyāṇi mano buddhirasyādhiṣṭhānamucyate
etairvimohayatyeṣa jñānamāvṛtya dehinam
english_telang: The senses, the mind, and the understanding are said to be its seat with these it deludes the embodied (self) after enveloping knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
iast:
tasmāttvamindriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣabha
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hyenaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam
english_telang: Therefore, O chief of the descendants of Bharata! first restrain your senses, then cast off this sinful thing which destroys knowledge and experience.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
iast:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhurindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ
manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
english_telang: It has been said, Great are the senses, greater than the senses is the mind, greater than the mind is the understanding. What is greater than the understanding is that.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
iast:
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānamātmanā
jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam
english_telang: Thus knowing that which is higher than the understanding, and restraining (your)self by (your)self, O you of mighty arms! destroy this unmanageable enemy in the shape of desire.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam
vivasvānmanave prāha manurikṣvākave.abravīt
english_telang: This everlasting (system of) devotion I declared to the sun, the sun declared it to Manu , and Manu communicated it to Ikṣvāku. Coming thus by steps

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
iast:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa
english_telang: it became known to royal sages. But O terror of (your) foes! that devotion was lost to the world by long (lapse of) time. That same primeval devotion I have declared to you to-day

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
iast:
sa evāyaṃ mayā te.adya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto.asi me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam
english_telang: seeing. that you are my devotee and friend for it is the highest mystery.

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti
english_telang: Later is your birth the birth of the sun is prior. How then shall I understand that you declared (this) first?

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa
english_telang: I have passed through many births, O Arjuna I and you also. I know them all, but you, O terror of (your) foes! do not know them.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥
iast:
ajo.api sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro.api san
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmyātmamāyayā
english_telang: Even though I am unborn and inexhaustible in (my) essence even though I am lord of all beings still I take up the control of my own nature and am born by means of my delusive power.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
iast:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham
english_telang: Whensoever, O descendant of Bharata! piety languishes, and impiety is in the ascendant, I create myself.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥
iast:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
english_telang: I am born age after age, for the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, and the establishment of piety.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
iast:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so.arjuna
english_telang: Whoever truly knows thus my divine birth and work, casts off (this) body and is not born again. He comes to me O Arjuna! Many from whom affection

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
iast:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ
english_telang: fear

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
iast:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
english_telang: and wrath have departed who are full of me who depend on me and who are purified by the penance of knowledge have come into my essence. I serve men in the way in which they approach me. In every way, O son of Pṛthā! men follow in my path.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
iast:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā
english_telang: Desiring the success of actions, men in this world worship the divinities, for in this world of mortals, the success produced by action is soon obtained.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
iast:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam
english_telang: The fourfold division of castes was created by me according to the apportionment of qualities and duties. But though I am its author know me to be inexhaustible and not the author.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
iast:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā
iti māṃ yo.abhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate
english_telang: Actions defile me not. I have no attachment to the fruit of actions. He who knows me thus is not tied down by actions.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
iast:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam
english_telang: Knowing this, the men of old who wished for final emancipation, performed action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
iast:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo.apyatra mohitāḥ
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase.aśubhāt
english_telang: Therefore do you, too, perform action as was done by men of old in olden times. Even sages are confused as to what is action, what inaction. Therefore I will speak to you about action, and learning that, you will be freed from (this world of) evil. One must possess knowledge about action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
iast:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
english_telang: one must also possess knowledge about prohibited action and again one must possess knowledge about inaction. The truth regarding action is abstruse.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
iast:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ
sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
english_telang: He is wise among men, he is possessed of devotion, and performs all actions, who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
iast:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ
english_telang: The wise call him learned, whose acts are all free from desires and fancies, and whose actions are burnt down by the fire of knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
iast:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto.api naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ
english_telang: Forsaking all attachment to the fruit of action, always contented, dependent on none, he does nothing at all, though he engages in action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
iast:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
english_telang: Devoid of expectations, restraining the mind and the self, and casting off all belongings, he incurs no sin, performing actions merely for the sake of the body.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
iast:
yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
english_telang: Satisfied with earnings coming spontaneously rising above the pairs of opposites free from all animosity and equable on success or ill-success he is not fettered down even though he performs (actions).

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥
iast:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate
english_telang: The acts of one who is devoid of attachment who is free whose mind is fixed on knowledge and who performs action for (the purpose of) the sacrifice are all destroyed.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
iast:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā
english_telang: Brahman is the oblation with Brahman (as a sacrificial instrument) it is offered up Brahman is in the fire and by Brahman it is thrown

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
iast:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati
english_telang: and Brahman, too, is the goal to which he proceeds who meditates on Brahman in the action. Some devotees perform the sacrifice to the gods, some offer up the sacrifice by the sacrifice itself in the fire of Brahman.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
iast:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
english_telang: Others offer up the senses, such as the sense of hearing and others, in the fires of restraint others offer up the objects of sense, such as sound and so forth, into the fires of the senses.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
iast:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite
english_telang: Some again offer up all the operations of the senses and the operations of the life-breaths into the fire of devotion by self-restraint, kindled by knowledge. Others perform the sacrifice of wealth the sacrifice of penance the sacrifice of concentration of mind

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥
iast:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english_telang: the sacrifice of Vedic study and of knowledge and others are ascetics of rigid vows.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
iast:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe.apānaṃ tathāpare
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ
english_telang: Some offer up the upward life-breath into the downward life-breath and the downward life-breath into the upper life-breath and stopping up the motions of the upward and downward life-breaths devote themselves to the restraint of the life-breaths.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥
iast:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati
sarve.apyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ
english_telang: Others, who (take) limited food, offer up the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All of these, conversant with the sacrifice, have their sins destroyed by the sacrifice.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥
iast:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam
nāyaṃ loko.astyayajñasya kuto.anyaḥ kurusattama
english_telang: Those who eat the nectar-like leavings of the sacrifice repair to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for those who perform no sacrifice, whence (then) the other, O best of the Kauravas!

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
iast:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase
english_telang: Thus sacrifices of various sorts are laid down in the Vedas . Know them all to be produced from action, and knowing this you will be released (from the fetters of this world). The sacrifice of knowledge O terror of (your) foes! is superior to the sacrifice of wealth for action

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
iast:
śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
english_telang: O son of Pṛthā! is wholly and entirely comprehended in knowledge. That you should learn by salutation question

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
iast:
tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ
english_telang: and service. The men of knowledge who perceive the truth will teach knowledge to you.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि (var अशेषाणि) ॥
iast:
yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava
yena bhūtānyaśeṣāṇi drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi
english_telang: Having learnt that, O son of Pāṇḍu! you will not again fall thus into delusion and by means of it, you will see all beings, without exception, first in yourself, and then in me.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
iast:
api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi
english_telang: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinful men

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
iast:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho.agnirbhasmasātkurute.arjuna
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā
english_telang: you will cross over all trespasses by means of the boat of knowledge alone. As a fire well kindled O Arjuna! reduces fuel to ashes

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
iast:
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
english_telang: so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes. For there is in this world no means of sanctification like knowledge and that one perfected by devotion finds within one's self in time.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
śraddhāvā.Nllabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati
english_telang: He who has faith, whose senses are restrained, and who is assiduous, obtains knowledge. Obtaining knowledge, he acquires, without delay, the highest tranquillity.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
iast:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati
nāyaṃ loko.asti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ
english_telang: He who is ignorant and devoid of faith, and whose self is full of misgivings, is ruined. Not this world, not the next, nor happiness, is for him whose self is full of misgivings.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम्।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥
iast:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
english_telang: Actions, O Dhanañjaya ! do not fetter one who is self-possessed, who has renounced action by devotion, and who has destroyed misgivings by knowledge.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
iast:
tasmādajñānasambhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata
english_telang: Therefore, O descendant of Bharata! destroy, with the sword of knowledge, these misgivings of yours which fill your mind, and which are produced from ignorance. Engage in devotion. Arise!

speaker: Arjuna
devanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच।
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम् ॥
iast:
arjuna uvāca
saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi
yacchreya etayorekaṃ tanme brūhi suniścitam
english_telang: O Kṛṣṇa ! you praise renunciation of actions and also the pursuit (of them). Tell me determinately which one of these two is superior.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaśca niḥśreyasakarāvubhau
tayostu karmasaṃnyāsātkarmayogo viśiṣyate
english_telang: Renunciation and pursuit of action are both instruments of happiness. But of the two, pursuit of action is superior to renunciation of action.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
iast:
jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati
nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhātpramucyate
english_telang: He should be understood to be always an ascetic who has no aversion and no desire. For O you of mighty arms! he who is free from the pairs of opposites is easily released from (all) bonds.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ॥
iast:
sāṅkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam
english_telang: Children—not wise men—talk of saṅkhya and yoga as distinct. One who pursues either well obtains the fruit of both.

speaker: Krishna
devanagari:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति ॥
iast:
yatsāṅkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tadyogairapi gamyate
ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
